claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're enquiring about, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm inquiring about my child Alex. He's 17 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a bit more about his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or certain vocational qualifications) or approved training (such as an unpaid training course)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he's not doing A-levels or anything like that, but he has just started an apprenticeship. Does that count?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. I have an important follow-up question about Alex's apprenticeship.

Is Alex's apprenticeship based in England? The reason I ask is that apprenticeships in England affect Child Benefit eligibility differently than those elsewhere in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - his apprenticeship is in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, I have to share some news that may not be what you were hoping for. Based on the information you've provided, you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Reason:**

Although Alex is 17 and lives with you (which would normally meet the basic eligibility criteria), the rules state that Child Benefit stops when a child starts an **apprenticeship in England**. Since Alex has begun an apprenticeship in England, this specifically disqualifies you from receiving Child Benefit for him.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he leaves the apprenticeship and returns to approved education or training—you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old, which means he falls into the 16-19 age category where continued Child Benefit eligibility depends on remaining in approved education or training. While Alex lives with his parent (meeting the responsibility criteria), he has started an apprenticeship in England. Under the Child Benefit rules, a child starting an apprenticeship in England causes Child Benefit payments to stop. This is specifically stated in the rules: 'You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship in England.' Therefore, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
